gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Sony's own US manuals rate the 120 W HT-S100F and the 330 W HT-SD40 at the same 20 W per channel minimum RMS (FTC, ≤1% THD). The headline totals are sums of 'reference' figures measured at a single frequency, and both bars receive Bluetooth over SBC only.
standout_why: I read geekchamp.com 'Best Bluetooth TV Speakers in 2026: 5 Soundbars' (ranked #3/#4). For its five soundbars it gives no wattage, Bluetooth version or codec. Its only wattage advice is 'Choose based on the room and speaker layout, not a wattage label.' Its only latency figure is a second-hand PCWorld 'up to about 150 ms' with no codec for the picks. None of its picks are the Sony or Samsung bars ChatGPT showed. The cited itechguides connection guide and itechguides #1 timed out twice. What Hi-Fi's page came back truncated, so I could not check those three. The gap claim rests on geekchamp plus ChatGPT's own answers, which quote no rated power or codec.
decides: This confirms the cheap pick and changes why you'd pay more. The $229 HT-SD40's 330 W against the HT-S100F's 120 W does not mean a louder bar. Both are rated 20 W per channel minimum RMS under FTC rules. The difference is mostly the SD40's 130 W (reference) subwoofer, so pay the extra only for bass. Both use SBC-only Bluetooth receivers, and the Samsung B630F's 'Bluetooth TV Connection' works only with Samsung TVs. For a lag-free TV link, use the HDMI ARC or optical input, which every candidate has. Don't count on Bluetooth from the TV. Samsung's own spec page lists no output wattage, only 24 W (bar) + 48 W (sub) operating power consumption. That makes the 370 W retail claim impossible to compare with the Sony figures.

findings.label: US FTC rated power (front L+R)
findings.value: 20 W per channel minimum RMS (40 W total), 8 ohms, both channels driven, 100–5,000 Hz, ≤1% THD
findings.source_title: Sony HT-S100F Operating Instructions, p. 32 Specifications (ManualsLib copy)
findings.note: Sony's own operating instructions, Amplifier section for US models: 'rated 20 W per channel minimum RMS power, with no more than 1% total harmonic distortion from 250 mW to rated output.'

findings.label: Reference power output (source of the '120 W' headline)
findings.value: 30 W woofer blocks per channel (8 ohms, 1 kHz) + 30 W tweeter blocks per channel (8 ohms, 10 kHz) = 120 W
findings.source_title: Sony HT-S100F Operating Instructions, p. 32 Specifications (ManualsLib copy)
findings.note: Arithmetic: 4 × 30 W = 120 W. These are single-frequency reference figures with no THD limit. 120 W ÷ 40 W FTC = 3× inflation.

findings.source_title: Sony HT-S100F Operating Instructions, p. 32 Specifications (ManualsLib copy)
findings.note: Inputs on the same page: HDMI OUT (TV (ARC)), TV IN (OPTICAL), USB.

findings.label: US FTC rated power (front L+R)
findings.value: 20 W per channel minimum RMS, 4 ohms, both channels driven, 200–20,000 Hz, ≤1% THD
findings.source_title: Sony HT-SD40 Operating Instructions, p. 25 Specifications (ManualsLib copy)
findings.note: Same 20 W/ch minimum RMS as the HT-S100F. The load (4 ohms against 8 ohms) and frequency band differ, so this is the closest like-for-like figure Sony publishes.

findings.label: Reference power output (source of the '330 W' headline)
findings.value: 100 W per channel front L/R (4 ohms, 1 kHz) + 130 W subwoofer (4 ohms, 100 Hz) = 330 W
findings.source_title: Sony HT-SD40 Operating Instructions, p. 25 Specifications (ManualsLib copy)
findings.note: Arithmetic: 100 + 100 + 130 = 330 W. 130 of the 330 W (39%) is the subwoofer. Front reference against FTC: 100 W ÷ 20 W = 5× inflation.
